note: Flavour text as lore. Sourced by definition — it is printed on the card, so quoting it is quoting the object. Deduplicated by TEXT and kept at first printing, because reprints carry identical wording and a collection without that shows the same story three times.
method: Collections are only named where I read the matches. A first pass bucketed everything into six moods and every bucket leaked — 'amazing muscles' as sinister, 'doggedly pursues' as lonely. Precise categories are small; broad ones are noise.

lore-grim.name: The dark ones
lore-grim.hook: Which of these did you not know was this grim?
lore-grim.why: Cards whose own flavour text is genuinely unsettling — devouring, dragging away, feeding on dreams. Read and confirmed, not pattern-matched.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.lore: This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.

cards.name: Lunala ◇
cards.lore: Said to live in another world, this Pokémon devours light, drawing the moonless dark veil of night over the brightness of day.

cards.name: Trevenant
cards.lore: People fear it due to a belief that it devours any who try to cut down trees in its forest, but to the Pokémon it shares its woods with, it's kind.

cards.name: Hydreigon
cards.lore: It responds to movement by attacking. This scary, three-headed Pokémon devours everything in its path!

cards.name: Whiscash
cards.lore: A glutton that devours anything that moves, it quietly lurks at the bottom of swamps, lying in wait for prey.

cards.name: Solgaleo
cards.lore: In writings from the distant past, it's called by the name "the beast that devours the sun."

cards.name: Drowzee
cards.lore: It puts its prey to sleep and devours their dreams. It seems that bad dreams taste sour, so Drowzee doesn't particularly like eating them.

lore-sad.name: The sad ones
lore-sad.hook: Read the card. Then tell me it's a kids' game.
lore-sad.why: Flavour text about grief and loss, printed on cards sold to children. Cubone weeping for its dead mother is the canonical one.

cards.name: Cubone
cards.lore: It always wears the skull of its dead mother, so no one has any idea what its hidden face looks like.

cards.name: Cubone
cards.lore: The skull it wears on its head is that of its dead mother. According to some, it will evolve when it comes to terms with the pain of her death.

cards.name: Cubone
cards.lore: When it thinks of its dead mother, it cries. Its crying makes the skull it wears rattle hollowly.

cards.name: Cubone
cards.lore: At night, it weeps loudly for its dead mother, but those cries only attract its natural enemy—Mandibuzz.

cards.name: Cubone
cards.lore: When it thinks of its deceased mother, it weeps loudly. Mandibuzz that hear its cries will attack it from the air.

cards.name: Cubone
cards.lore: This Pokémon wears the skull of its deceased mother. Sometimes Cubone's dreams make it cry, but each tear Cubone sheds makes it stronger.

lore-cosmic.name: Not from here
lore-cosmic.hook: Which of these is actually an alien?
lore-cosmic.why: Cards whose text places them outside this world — another dimension, light-years, fell from the sky.

cards.name: Gastly
cards.lore: A mysterious Pokémon. Some say it is a lifeform from another dimension, while other believe it is formed from smog.

cards.name: Gothitelle
cards.lore: Starry skies thousands of light-years away are visible in the space distorted by their intense psychic power.

cards.name: Haunter
cards.lore: Because of its ability to slip through block walls, it is said to be from another dimension.

lore-absurd.name: Numbers that cannot be real
lore-absurd.hook: Pick the most ridiculous stat here.
lore-absurd.why: Flavour text making a specific, checkable, impossible claim. A 5000 IQ. Moving a mountain. It is the specificity that makes it funny.

cards.name: Flareon
cards.lore: When storing thermal energy in its body, its temperature could soar to over 1600 degrees.

cards.name: Alakazam
cards.lore: Its brain can outperform a supercomputer. Its intelligence quotient is said to be 5000.

cards.name: Light Flareon
cards.lore: It creates its flames by swallowing air into a special pouch within its body, then heating it to over 3000 degrees.

cards.name: Rapidash
cards.lore: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.

cards.name: Rapidash
cards.lore: It gallops at nearly 150 mph. With its mane blazing ferociously, it races as if it were an arrow.

cards.name: Rhydon
cards.lore: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3600 degrees.

cards.name: Galarian Zapdos
cards.lore: One kick from its powerful legs will pulverize a dump truck. Supposedly, this Pokémon runs through the mountains at over 180 mph.

cards.name: Onix
cards.lore: When it travels underground, it causes rumbling and tremors. It can move at 50 mph.

cards.name: Tornadus
cards.lore: The lower half of its body is wrapped in a cloud of energy. It zooms through the sky at 200 mph.

cards.name: Skarmory
cards.lore: Its heavy-looking iron body is actually thin and light, so it can fly at speeds over 180 mph.

cards.name: Skarmory
cards.lore: Despite being clad entirely in iron-hard armor, it flies at speeds over 180 mph.

cards.name: Pupitar
cards.lore: Its shell is as hard as sheet rock, and it is also very strong. Its thrashing can topple a mountain.

cards.name: Skarmory
cards.lore: Despite being clad entirely in iron-hard armor, it flies at speed of over 180 mph.

cards.name: Kakuna
cards.lore: Although it is a cocoon, it can move a little. It can extend its poison barb if it is attacked.

cards.name: Gastly
cards.lore: A being that exists as a thin gas. It can topple an Indian elephant by enveloping the prey in two seconds.

cards.name: Talonflame
cards.lore: When attacking prey, it can reach speeds of up to 310 mph. It finishes its prey off with a colossal kick.

cards.name: Clawitzer
cards.lore: By expelling water from the nozzle in the back of its claw, it can move at a speed of 60 knots.

cards.name: Drakloak
cards.lore: It's capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.

cards.name: Espathra
cards.lore: It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph.

lore.base2-3: When storing thermal energy in its body, its temperature could soar to over 1600 degrees.

lore.base2-38: Its tongue can be extended like a chameleon's. It leaves a stinging sensation when it licks enemies.

lore.base2-45: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3600 degrees.

lore.base2-55: Extremely quick to anger. It could be docile one moment, then thrashing away the next.

lore.base2-57: Although small, its venomous barbs make this Pokémon dangerous. The female has smaller horns.

lore.base2-63: Lives in the shadows of tall trees where it eats insects. It is attracted by light at night.

lore.basep-4: When several of these Pokémon gather, they attract so much electricity that they can cause lightning to strike.

lore.basep-6: A legendary Pokémon famous for its beauty. It looks almost as if it flies when it runs.
lore.basep-8: So rare that it is still said to be a mirage by many experts. Only a few people have seen it worldwide.
lore.basep-17: Popular with women because of its beautiful fur. The leader of the Rockets keeps one as a pet.
lore.basep-18: This Pokémon is more active at night. It likes bright, shiny things and cannot resist taking them and adding them to its collection.
lore.basep-20: While lulling its enemies with its vacant look, this wily Pokémon will use psychokinetic powers.
lore.basep-21: The flames on this legendary Pokémon's wings burn so brightly that they can make night seem like day.
lore.basep-22: This legendary Pokémon is said to freeze the water in the air during winter, causing snow.
lore.basep-23: This legendary Pokémon is said to be present wherever there is a lightning storm.

lore.basep-28: One summer, a group of Pikachus was found riding the waves at the local beach.
lore.basep-29: The tip of its tail, which contains oil that is lighter than water, lets it swim without drowning.
lore.basep-30: Still only a hatchling, it uses poison to chase off its enemies when threatened.
lore.basep-31: Because of its unusual, star-like silhouette, people believe that it came here on a meteor.

lore.basep-33: Its wings are not used for flying. They are flapped at high speed to adjust its body temperature.

lore.basep-35: It is not yet skilled at storing electricity. It may send out a jolt if amused or startled.

lore.basep-45: With ninja-like agility and speed, it can create the illusion that there is more than one.
lore.basep-48: A legendary bird Pokémon that is said to appear to doomed people who are lost in icy mountains.

lore.bw6-101: It spends nearly all its time in a day sprawled out. Just seeing it makes one drowsy.
lore.bw6-102: Its heart beats at a tenfold tempo, so it cannot sit still for even a moment.
lore.bw6-103: The world's laziest Pokémon. When it is lounging, it is actually saving energy for striking back.

lore.bw6-109: They great one another by rubbing each other with their tails, which are always kept well groomed and clean.

lore.dp6-52: If its body takes on an aura, the weather changes instantly. It is said to live in seas and lakes.

lore.dp6-14: It lives in the ozone layer far above the clouds and cannot be seen from the ground.

lore.dp6-111: It often plants its root feet in the ground during the day and sows seeds as it walks about at night.

lore.bw7-26: It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.

lore.bw7-29: It shelters itself in its shell then strikes back with spouts of water at every opportunity.

lore.bw7-33: When headaches stimulate its brain cells, which are usually inactive, it can use a mysterious power.

lore.bw7-35: When its forehead shines mysteriously, Golduck can use the full extent of its power.

lore.bw7-37: Its long ears are superb sensors. It can distinguish the movements of things in water and tell what they are.
lore.bw7-38: It carries food all day long. When someone is lost in the mountains, it shares that food.
lore.bwp-BW03: It fights using the scalchop on its stomach. In response to an attack, it retaliates immediately by slashing.

lore.bw7-44: If its veil-like arms stun and wrap a foe, that foe will be dragged miles below the surface, never to return.

lore.bw7-47: It crosses the world, running over the surfaces of oceans and rivers. It appears at scenic waterfronts.
lore.bw7-48: By blasting water from its hooves, it can glide across water. It excels at using leg moves while battling.

lore.bw7-53: Research is progressing on storing lightning in Electabuzz so this energy can be used at any time.
lore.bw7-54: The instant it presses the tips of its tails onto an opponent, it sends over 20,000 volts of electricity into the foe.
lore.dp6-87: It discharges positive and negative electricity from its antenna tips to shock its foes.
lore.bw7-56: Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use the frequency and rhythm of these flashes to communicate.
lore.bw7-57: When this ill-tempered Pokémon runs wild, it shoots lightning from its mane in all directions.
lore.dp1-41: It desperately tries to keep its black tail hidden. It is said to be proof the tail hides a secret.
lore.bw7-59: Using its tail like a spring, it keeps its heart beating by bouncing constantly. If it stops, it dies.
lore.bw7-60: It uses black pearls to amplify its psychic power. It does a strange dance to control foes' minds.
lore.bw7-61: It loves the crying of children. It startles bad kids by passing through walls and making them cry.

lore.bw7-63: It is said to take lost spirits into its pliant body and guide them home.

lore.bw7-69: The dream mist coming from its forehead changes into many different colors depending on the dream that was eaten.
lore.bw7-70: The heart-shaped mark left on a body after a Woobat has been attached to it is said to bring good fortune.
lore.bw7-71: It shakes its tail vigorously when it emits ultrasonic waves strong enough to reduce concrete to rubble.
lore.bw7-72: Using the feelers on its head and tail, it picks up vibrations in the air to determine its prey's location and state.
lore.bw7-73: Storing energy for evolution, it sits. But, when predators approach, it moves to stab them with poison spikes.
lore.bw7-74: It clasps its prey with the claws on its neck until it stops moving. Then it finishes it off with deadly poison.
lore.bw7-75: Their ribbonlike feelers increase their psychic power. They are always staring at something.

lore.bw7-77: The melodies sung by Meloetta have the power to make Pokémon that hear them happy or sad.
lore.bw7-78: It digs deep burrows to live in. When in danger, it rolls up its body to withstand attacks.

lore.bw7-80: It clamps on to its chosen prey then jabs the stinger on its tail into the prey while it's stunned with surprise.
lore.bw7-81: It dances silently through the sky. When it approaches prey, it can land a critical hit in an instant.
lore.bw7-83: It makes an inescapable conical pit and lies in wait at the bottom for prey to come tumbling down.
lore.bw7-84: When it finds a stone of a suitable size, it secretes a liquid from its mouth to open up a hole to crawl into.
lore.bw7-85: When its boulder is broken in battles for territory, it feels unsure and begins to weaken.

lore.bw7-91: Their beautiful form comes from the muscles they have developed. They run silently in the night.

lore.bw7-94: It raises its pincers with eyelike markings for intimidation. It also swings them down dangerously.
lore.bw7-95: Despite being clad entirely in iron-hard armor, it flies at speed of over 180 mph.

lore.bw7-97: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.
lore.bw7-98: The ultrasonic waves it generates by rubbing its two wings together cause severe headaches.
lore.bw7-99: Known as "The Desert Spirit" this Pokémon hides in the sandstorms it causes by beating its wings.
lore.bwp-BW58: This legendary ice Pokémon waits for a hero to fill in the missing parts of its body with truth or ideals.
lore.bw7-104: It searches for food all day. It gnaws on hard objects to wear down its fangs, which grow constantly during its lifetime.
lore.bw7-105: With its long fangs, this surprisingly violent Pokémon can gnaw away even thick concrete with ease.
lore.bw7-108: It can reconstitute its entire cellular structure to change into what it sees, but it returns to normal when it relaxes.
lore.bw7-109: When its belly is full, it becomes too lethargic to even lift a finger, so it is safe to bounce on its belly.
lore.bw7-110: It transforms the kindness and joy of others into happiness, which it stores in its shell.

lore.bw7-113: It shows its cute side by chasing its own tail until it gets dizzy.
lore.bw7-114: The reason it does not have a nest is that it simply searches for a clean, comfortable place then sleeps there.
lore.bw7-116: By extending its rolled up ears and striking the ground, it can bound so high it surprises itself.
lore.bw7-117: Extremely cautious, it quickly bounds off when it senses danger.
lore.bw7-118: Extremely cautious, one of them will always be on the lookout, but it won't notice a foe coming from behind.
lore.bw7-119: Using luminescent matter, it makes its eyes and body glow and stuns attacking opponents.
lore.bw7-120: Though it is a very brave Pokémon, it's also smart enough to check its foe's strength and avoid battle.
lore.bw7-121: This very loyal Pokémon helps trainers, and it also takes care of other Pokémon.
lore.bw7-122: Being wrapped in its long fur is so comfortable that a person would be fine even overnight on a wintry mountain.
lore.bw7-123: This very forgetful Pokémon will wait for a new order from its Trainer even though it already has one.

lore.bw7-125: Males swing the plumage on their heads to threaten others, but females are better at flying.
lore.bw7-126: Using the feelers on its ears, it can tell how someone is feeling or when an egg might hatch.
lore.dp6-105: It lived on the seafloor 100 million years ago and was reanimated scientifically.
lore.dp6-21: It lives in the shallows of warm seas. When the tide goes out, it digs up prey from beaches.
lore.bw10-5: It flies by flapping its broad leaves and gives the sweet, delicious fruit around its neck to children.
lore.bw10-6: For some reason they evolve when they receive electrical energy while they are attacking Shelmet.
lore.bw10-7: When it and Karrablast are together, and both receive electrical stimulation, they both evolve.
lore.bw10-8: When its body dries out, it weakens. So it wraps a membrane around itself for protection while it spits poison.
lore.bwp-BW86: This Pokémon existed 300 million years ago. Team Plasma altered it and attached a cannon to its back.
lore.bw10-12: Said to have been born from the sun, it spews fire from its horns and encases itself in a cocoon of fire when it evolves.

lore.bw10-17: Able to understand human speech and very intelligent, it loves to swim in the sea with people on its back.
lore.bw10-18: The water they shoot from their mouths can hit moving prey from more than 300 feet away.
lore.bw10-19: It has a tendency to want to be in holes. It prefers rock crags or pots and sprays ink from them before attacking.
lore.bw10-21: It is said that several Snorunt gather under giant leaves and live together in harmony.
lore.bw10-22: It prevents prey from escaping by instantaneously freezing moisture in the air.
lore.bw10-23: It freezes prey by blowing its -58 degrees F breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.
lore.bw10-25: Seemingly curious about people, they gather around footsteps they find on snowy mountains.
lore.bw10-26: They appear when the snow flowers bloom. When the petals fall, they retreat to places unknown again.
lore.bw10-27: This Pokémon was restored from a fossil. It swam skillfully and dove to depths beyond half a mile.
lore.bw10-28: It could knock out a foe with a slap from one of its developed front appendages and chew it up, shell or bones and all.

lore.bw10-46: Golurk were created to protect people and Pokémon. They run on a mysterious energy.

lore.bw10-54: It runs better than it flies. It takes off into the sky by running at a speed of 25 mph.

lore.bw10-58: Lairon fight over territory, and when their steel bodies collide, sparks fly.
lore.bw10-59: It claims an entire mountain as its own. The more wounds it has, the more it has battled, so don't take it lightly.
lore.bw10-61: Wearing the shell covering they stole from Shelmet, they defend themselves and attack with two lances.
lore.bw10-67: Its large tusks have a tendency to break, but each time they grow back, they grow in harder and sturdier.

lore.bw10-71: It raises its offspring in its belly pouch. It lets the baby play only when it feels safe.

lore.bw10-73: It was upgraded to enable the exploration of other planets. However, it failed to measure up.
lore.bwp-BW84: Its programming was modified to enable work in alien dimensions. It did not work as planned.

lore.bw10-76: In its territory, it leaves scratches on trees that bear delicious berries or fruits.
lore.xy1-3: Often found in forests and grasslands. It has a sharp, toxic barb of around two inches on top of its head.
lore.xy1-4: Almost incapable of moving, this Pokémon can only harden its shell to protect itself when it is in danger.
lore.xy1-5: It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.

lore.xy1-11: It attacks enemies with strikes of its thorn-covered tail. This Pokémon is wild tempered.

lore.bw8-19: Very intelligent, it roasts berries before eating them. It likes to help people.

lore.xy1-33: Even if its body is torn, it can regenerate as long as the glowing central core remains intact.

lore.xy1-38: The high-pressure water expelled from its tail is so powerful, it can destroy a concrete wall.
lore.xy1-39: It secretes flexible bubbles from its chest and back. The bubbles reduce the damage it would otherwise take when attacked.
lore.xy1-40: It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with precise control, hitting empty cans up to a hundred feet away.
lore.xy1-41: It creates throwing stars out of compressed water. When it spins them and throws them at high speed, these stars can split metal in two.
lore.xy1-44: It was discovered when Poké Balls were introduced. It is said that there is some connection.
lore.xy1-45: It explodes in response to even minor stimuli. It is feared, with the nickname of "The Bomb Ball."
lore.xy1-47: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.
lore.xy1-48: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.
lore.dp6-121: It bounces constantly, using its tail like a spring. The shock of bouncing keeps its heart beating.
lore.xy1-51: It discovers what is going on around it by using the feelers on its head and tail. It is brutally aggressive.
lore.xy1-52: Protected by a hard shell, it spins its body like a wheel and crashes furiously into its enemies.
lore.xy1-54: These Pokémon are created when spirits possess rotten tree stumps. They prefer to live in abandoned forests.

lore.xy1-56: The pumpkin body is inhabited by a spirit trapped in this world. As the sun sets, it becomes restless and active.
lore.xy1-57: Singing in eerie voices, they wander town streets on the night of the new moon. Anyone who hears their song is cursed.

lore.xy1-59: In battle, it digs through the ground and strikes the unsuspecting foe from an unexpected direction.

lore.xy1-61: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit.

lore.bw8-80: With strengthened bodies, they skillfully wield steel beams to take down buildings.

lore.xy1-69: It moves along below the sand's surface, except for its nose and eyes. A dark membrane shields its eyes from the sun.
lore.xy1-71: Very violent Pokémon, they try to clamp down on anything that moves in front of their eyes.
lore.xy1-72: It changes so it looks like its foe, tricks it, and then uses that opportunity to flee.
lore.bwp-BW09: Each has the ability to fool a large group of people simultaneously. They protect their lair with illusory scenery.
lore.xy1-74: Opponents who stare at the flashing of the light-emitting spots on its body become dazed and lose their will to fight.
lore.xy1-76: It wields the most compelling hypnotic powers of any Pokémon, and it forces others to do whatever it wants.
lore.xy1-78: When this legendary Pokémon's wings and tail feathers spread wide and glow red, it absorbs the life force of all living creatures.

lore.xy1-87: It captivates foes with its huge, round eyes, then lulls them to sleep by singing a soothing melody.

lore.xy1-91: Emanations from its fingertips solidify the air into invisible walls that repel even harsh attacks.
lore.xy1-92: It emits a scent that enraptures those who smell it. This fragrance changes depending on what it has eaten.

lore.sm7-79: It is said that it originates from clay dolls made by an ancient civilization.

lore.dp6-31: It is said to have the ability to grant any wish for just one week every thousand years.

lore.sm7-103: With its steel-hard stone head, it headbutts indiscriminately. This is because of the stress it feels at being unable to fly.

lore.sm8-106: One of the Ultra Beasts, it's unclear whether or not this Pokémon is sentient, but sometimes it can be observed behaving like a young girl.

lore.sm8-110: Apparently, the larger the green parts of this Pokémon, the more collectors value it. It's a particular favorite among elderly people.
lore.sm8-113: If you are enchanted by its smooth, dance-like kicks, you may get a closer experience with one than you'd like.

lore.sm12-130: There are a hundred or so of them living in Alola's waste-disposal site. They're all hard workers who eat a lot of trash.
lore.sm12-131: There are over a hundred kinds of poison inside its body. Chemical reactions between different poisons are the source of its vitality.
lore.sm12-133: The only thing unlucky about Absol is its appearance. It protects fields and warns people of disaster, so one ought to be grateful for it.
lore.sm12-134: After shredding its prey, it sharpens its blades on a stone by the river. Each Pawniard has its own favorite sharpening stone.
lore.sm12-135: No matter how strong the Bisharp, it's said that if the blade on its head is chipped, it will retire from its position as the boss.
lore.sm12-137: After fleeing a volcanic eruption, it ended up moving to an area of snowy mountains. Its ice shell is as hard as steel.
lore.sm12-138: It runs across snow-covered plains at high speeds. It developed thick, sharp claws to plow through the snow.
lore.sm12-140: A cunning and terrifying Pokémon, its cuteness makes opponents let down their guard—and then it swallows them whole with its huge jaws.
lore.sm12-141: Although it can control its units known as Mini-Noses, they sometimes get lost and don't come back.
lore.sm12-142: Sometimes the result of its opening an Ultra Wormhole is that energy and life-forms from other worlds are called here to this world.
lore.sm12-145: The reason it guides people all the way down to the mountain's base is that it wants them to hurry up and leave.
lore.dp1-69: A Pokémon that lives by water. It moves quickly on land by bouncing on its big tail.
lore.sm12-148: This nuisance sneaks into people's homes, where it hides important things and scatters cotton all over the place.
lore.sm12-149: It's not safe without the power of a flower, but it will keep traveling around until it finds one with the color and shape it wants.
lore.sm12-151: It raises flowers and uses them as weapons. The more gorgeous the blossom, the more power it contains.
lore.sm12-152: It controls the flowers it grows. The petal blizzards that Florges triggers are overwhelming in their beauty and power.
lore.mcd14-9: To entangle its opponents in battle, it extrudes white threads as sweet and sticky as cotton candy.
lore.sm12-155: Once a fight breaks out, it will unflinchingly charge at dragon Pokémon that are many times larger than itself.
lore.sm12-159: If a child it has made friends with is bullied, Drampa will find the bully's house and burn it to the ground.
lore.sm12-160: It smacks the scales on its head against rocks or against the ground to frighten its opponents. It can also contact its friends with these noises.
lore.sm12-162: It makes noise by clanging its scales together. When the rhythm has reached its peak, Hakamo-o attacks.
lore.sm12-163: When it howls after finishing off its prey, the metallic sounds of its celebrating comrades can be heard from all around.
lore.smp-SM165: This is its form when it has absorbed overwhelming light energy. It fires laser beams from all over its body.
lore.smp-SM235: The question of why only Eevee has such unstable genes has still not been solved.
lore.sm12-168: It's always practicing its singing because it wants to improve. Even when it's asleep, it keeps singing in its dreams!
lore.smp-SM244: As it did more and more with its tail, its hands became clumsy. It makes its nest high in the treetops.
lore.sm12-170: In their search for comfortable trees, they get into territorial disputes with groups of Passimian. They win about half the time.
lore.sm12-172: With its ability to distinguish any aroma, it unfailingly finds all food buried deep underground.
lore.sm12-174: This Pokémon has excellent judgment. If it decides it can't defeat an opponent, it immediately turns tail and vamooses.
lore.sm12-175: The longer its black fur grows, the harder and more impervious it gets. Claws and fangs can't easily penetrate it.
lore.sm12-176: It pays no mind to the cold, thanks to its long warm coat. Stoutland in Alola look a little uncomfortable.
lore.sm12-177: With its powerful legs and sturdy claws, it can crack even the hard shells of Shellder and pluck out their insides.
lore.sm12-178: The more scars it has on its front, the more heroic it's considered to be. Those with many scars on their back are mocked by the flock.
lore.sm12-181: It boasts power enough to split large trees in half. The organ on its rear releases an odor that it uses to communicate with others of its kind.
lore.sm12-182: It waves its hands wildly in intimidation and warning. Life is over for anyone who doesn't run away as fast as possible.
lore.sm12-183: A Pokémon weapon developed for a specific mission, it went berserk during an experiment, so it was cryogenically frozen.
lore.swsh1-2: Its flowers give off a relaxing fragrance. The stronger its aroma, the healthier the Roselia is.
lore.swsh1-4: After captivating opponents with its sweet scent, it lashes them with its thorny whips.
lore.swsh1-5: It shoots cotton from its body to protect itself. If it gets caught up in hurricane-strength winds, it can get sent to the other side of the Earth.
lore.swsh1-6: It scatters cotton all over the place as a prank. If it gets wet, it'll become too heavy to move and have no choice but to answer for its mischief.
lore.swsh1-7: With noises that could be mistaken for the rattles of maracas, it creates an upbeat rhythm, startling bird Pokémon and making them fly off in a hurry.
lore.swsh1-8: They lay their eggs deep inside their nests. When attacked by Heatmor, they retaliate using their massive mandibles.
lore.swshp-SWSH001: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.
lore.swsh1-12: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.
lore.swshp-SWSH006: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.
lore.swsh1-16: Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.
lore.swsh1-17: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn't.
lore.swsh1-18: As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.
lore.swsh1-19: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what's around it—and what's around it can include things over six miles away.
lore.swsh1-20: It whirls around in the wind while singing a joyous song. This delightful display has charmed many into raising this Pokémon.
lore.swshp-SWSH046: The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.
lore.swsh1-23: It is said to live 1,000 years, and each of its tails is loaded with supernatural powers.
lore.swsh1-26: There's a hole in its tail that allows it to draw in the air it needs to keep its fire burning. If the hole gets blocked, this Pokémon will fall ill.
lore.swsh1-27: Its venom sacs produce a fluid that this Pokémon then heats up with the flame in its tail. This process creates Salandit's poisonous gas.
lore.swsh1-28: Only female Salazzle exist. They emit a gas laden with pheromones to captivate male Salandit.
lore.swsh1-29: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.
lore.swshp-SWSH244: It has special pads on the backs of its feet, and one on its nose. Once it's raring to fight, these pads radiate tremendous heat.
lore.swshp-SWSH002: A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon's body. Once that happens, it's ready to fight at full power.
lore.swsh1-32: It kicks berries right off the branches of trees and then juggles them with its feet, practicing its footwork.
lore.swsh1-33: Its thick and fluffy fur protects it from the cold and enables it to use hotter fire moves.
lore.swshp-SWSH112: It's skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.
lore.swsh1-35: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.
lore.swsh1-37: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.
lore.swshp-SWSH048: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.
lore.swsh1-40: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell. It is surprisingly fast.
lore.swsh1-42: It can be found near the sea. The large pincers grow back if they are torn out of their sockets.
lore.swsh1-45: Its dorsal and pectoral fins are strongly developed like muscles. It can swim at a speed of five knots.
lore.swsh1-46: Its dorsal, pectoral, and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the Water Dancer.
lore.swshp-SWSH051: A smart and kindhearted Pokémon, it glides across the surface of the sea while its beautiful song echoes around it.
lore.swsh1-51: The small spikes covering its body developed from scales. They inject a toxin that causes fainting.
lore.swshp-SWSH026: If it builds up enough speed swimming, it can jump out above the waves and glide for over 300 feet.
lore.swshp-SWSH003: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won't be able to resist weeping.
lore.swsh1-56: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.
lore.swsh1-58: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.
lore.swsh1-60: It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.
lore.swshp-SWSH047: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.
lore.swsh1-62: It's so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it's battling midfight.
lore.swsh1-63: It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.
lore.swshp-SWSH007: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.
lore.swshp-SWSH020: Pikachu that can generate powerful electricity have cheek sacs that are extra soft and super stretchy.
lore.swsh1-68: Its antennae, which evolved from a fin, have both positive and negative charges flowing through them.
lore.swsh1-70: Joltik can be found clinging to other Pokémon. It's soaking up static electricity because it can't produce a charge on its own.
lore.swsh1-71: It launches electrified fur from its abdomen as its means of attack. Opponents hit by the fur could be in for three full days and nights of paralysis.
lore.swsh1-73: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.
lore.swsh1-75: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.
lore.swsh1-77: It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines.
lore.swshp-SWSH012: As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It's also generating electricity.
lore.swsh1-81: This Pokémon will look into your eyes and read the contents of your heart. If it finds evil there, it promptly hides away.
lore.swsh1-82: Brave and prideful, this Pokémon dashes airily through the forest, its steps aided by the psychic power stored in the fur on its fetlocks.
lore.swsh1-84: Its tongue is made of gas. If licked, its victim starts shaking constantly until death eventually comes.
lore.swshp-SWSH052: On the night of a full moon, if shadows move on their own and laugh, it must be Gengar's doing.
lore.swsh1-87: It eats dreams and releases mist. The mist is pink when it's eating a good dream, and black when it's eating a nightmare.
lore.swsh1-88: It drowses and dreams all the time. It's best to leave it be if it's just woken up, as it's a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.
lore.swsh1-89: This Pokémon is said to have been born when a lonely spirit possessed a cold, leftover cup of tea.
lore.swshp-SWSH081: This species lives in antique teapots. Most pots are forgeries, but on rare occasions, an authentic work is found.
lore.swsh1-92: If a Diglett digs through a field, it leaves the soil perfectly tilled and ideal for planting crops.
lore.swsh1-96: It can remember only one thing at a time. Once it starts rushing, it forgets why it started.
lore.swsh1-99: It relies on its carapace to deflect incoming attacks and throw its enemy off balance. As soon as that happens, it drives its drill into the foe.
lore.swsh1-100: If a tree branch shakes when there is no wind, it's a Sudowoodo, not a tree. It hides from the rain.
lore.swsh1-101: It moves while spinning around on its single foot. Some Baltoy have been seen spinning on their heads.
lore.swsh1-103: This mysterious Pokémon started life as an ancient clay figurine made over 20,000 years ago.
lore.swsh1-105: Loads weighing up to 50 times as much as its own body weight pose no issue for this Pokémon. It's skilled at making use of mud.
lore.swsh1-106: Mud that hardens around a Mudsdale's legs sets harder than stone. It's so hard that it allows this Pokémon to scrap a truck with a single kick.
lore.swsh1-107: It spews sand from its nostrils. While the enemy is blinded, it burrows into the ground to hide.
lore.swsh1-108: As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.
lore.swsh1-109: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.
lore.swsh1-110: When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.
lore.swsh1-111: It's very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.
lore.swsh1-113: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.
lore.swsh1-114: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun's descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.
lore.swsh1-117: Thought to be the oldest form of Zigzagoon, it moves in zigzags and wreaks havoc upon its surroundings.
lore.swsh1-118: This very aggressive Pokémon will recklessly challenge opponents stronger than itself.
lore.swshp-SWSH059: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.
lore.swsh1-121: It attacks using the claws on its tail. Once locked in its grip, its prey is unable to move as this Pokémon's poison seeps in.
lore.swsh1-122: It's so vicious that it's called the Sand Demon. Yet when confronted by Hippowdon, Drapion keeps a low profile and will never pick a fight.
lore.swsh1-123: It makes frightening noises with its poison-filled cheek sacs. When opponents flinch, Croagunk hits them with a poison jab.
lore.swsh1-124: It bounces toward opponents and gouges them with poisonous claws. No more than a scratch is needed to knock out its adversaries.
lore.swsh1-125: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.
lore.swsh1-126: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.
lore.swsh1-127: Living with a savage, seafaring people has toughened this Pokémon's body so much that parts of it have turned to iron.
lore.swshp-SWSH008: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.
lore.swsh1-130: It defends itself by launching spikes, but its aim isn't very good at first. Only after a lot of practice will it improve.
lore.swsh1-131: This Pokémon scrapes its spikes across rocks, and then uses the tips of its feelers to absorb the nutrients it finds within the stone.
lore.swsh1-132: Living in mud with a high iron content has given it a strong steel body.
lore.swsh1-133: A pack of these Pokémon forms to serve a Bisharp boss. Each Pawniard trains diligently, dreaming of one day taking the lead.
lore.swsh1-134: Violent conflicts erupt between Bisharp and Fraxure over places where sharpening stones can be found.
lore.swsh1-135: This Pokémon reigns supreme in the skies of the Galar region. The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.
lore.swsh1-136: If a job requires serious strength, this Pokémon will excel at it. Its copper body tarnishes in the rain, turning a vibrant green color.
lore.swsh1-137: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.
lore.swsh1-143: It begins to hoot at the same time every day. Some Trainers use them in place of clocks.
lore.swsh1-145: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.
lore.swsh1-147: Its body secretes oil that this Pokémon spreads over its nest as a coating to protect it from dust. Cinccino won't tolerate even a speck of the stuff.
lore.swsh1-148: It knows the forest inside and out. If it comes across a wounded Pokémon, Oranguru will gather medicinal herbs to treat it.
lore.swsh1-149: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.
lore.swsh1-150: It will bravely challenge any opponent, no matter how powerful. This Pokémon benefits from every battle—even a defeat increases its strength a bit.
lore.swsh1-151: Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.
lore.swsh1-152: If its fleece grows too long, Wooloo won't be able to move. Cloth made with the wool of this Pokémon is surprisingly strong.
lore.swshp-SWSH011: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.
lore.swsh1-154: Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.
lore.swsh3-11: At a distance, it launches its sharp feathers while flying about. If the enemy gets too close, Rowlet switches tactics and delivers vicious kicks.
lore.swsh3-12: It throws one knifelike feather after another at its enemies, and each one precisely strikes a weak point. These feathers are known as blade quills.
lore.swshp-SWSH035: As if wielding a bow, it launches the arrow quills hidden among the feathers of its wings. Decidueye's shots never miss.
lore.swsh2-20: It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it's just an apple and nothing more.
lore.swshp-SWSH022: It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns.
lore.swsh2-23: Eating a sweet apple caused its evolution. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on.
lore.swsh2-37: Its talent is tap-dancing. It can also manipulate temperatures to create a floor of ice, which this Pokémon can kick up to use as a barrier.
lore.swshp-SWSH079: It's highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.
lore.swsh2-47: It lived in snowy areas for so long that its fire sac cooled off and atrophied. It now has an organ that generates cold instead.
lore.swsh2-48: On days when blizzards blow through, it comes down to where people live. It stashes food in the snowball on its head, taking it home for later.
lore.swshp-SWSH093: If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It's very proud of that jaw.
lore.swsh2-53: This Pokémon has a jaw that's as sharp as a spear and as strong as steel. Apparently Barraskewda's flesh is surprisingly tasty, too.
lore.swsh45sv-SV033: It spits out thread imbued with a frigid sort of energy and uses it to tie its body to branches, disguising itself as an icicle while it sleeps.
lore.swsh2-54: It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold.
lore.swsh3-53: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.
lore.swsh3-54: Though it's able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.
lore.swsh45sv-SV038: One boy's invention led to the development of many different machines that take advantage of Rotom's unique capabilities.
lore.swsh2-68: It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows.
lore.swshp-SWSH137: When this Pokémon sounds as if it's strumming a guitar, it's actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity.
lore.swsh3-65: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.
lore.swshp-SWSH036: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.
lore.swsh2-78: Watch your step when wandering areas oceans once covered. What looks like a stone could be this Pokémon, and it will curse you if you kick it.
lore.swsh2-79: Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon's core spirit.
lore.swshp-SWSH080: Its upper whiskers are sensors that survey its surroundings. Its lower whiskers are organs that shoot electricity.
lore.swshp-SWSH040: Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures' emotions. If you don't have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you.
lore.swsh2-84: No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently.
lore.swsh2-85: It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.
lore.swsh2-86: This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream.
lore.swshp-SWSH058: When it trusts a Trainer, it will treat them to berries it's decorated with cream.
lore.swsh2-88: These intelligent Pokémon touch horns with each other to share information between them.
lore.swsh2-89: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.
lore.swsh2-90: It's capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.
lore.swsh2-91: When it isn't battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.
lore.swsh2-94: The Farfetch'd of the Galar region are brave warriors, and they wield thick, tough leeks in battle.
lore.swsh2-95: Only Farfetch'd that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon's leek withers, it will retire from combat.
lore.swsh2-101: A clay slab with cursed engravings took possession of a Yamask. The slab is said to be absorbing the Yamask's dark power.
lore.swsh2-102: A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move.
lore.swsh2-105: Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago.
lore.swsh2-106: It forms coal inside its body. Coal dropped by this Pokémon once helped fuel the lives of people in the Galar region.
lore.swshp-SWSH024: It's usually peaceful, but the vandalism of mines enrages it. Offenders will be incinerated with flames that reach 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit.
lore.swsh2-109: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass's orders are absolute.
lore.swsh2-112: Its body is full of poisonous gas. It floats into garbage dumps, seeking out the fumes of raw, rotting trash.
lore.swsh2-113: This Pokémon consumes particles that contaminate the air. Instead of leaving droppings, it expels clean air.
lore.swsh2-123: Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.
lore.swsh2-124: When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it's trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.
lore.swsh2-125: With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.
lore.swsh3-131: It digs up the ground with its trunk. It's also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all.
lore.swsh3-132: They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water.
lore.swshp-SWSH028: Its body resembles polished metal, and it's both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.
lore.swshp-SWSH082: It excels at digging holes. Using its ears, it can dig a nest 33 feet deep in one night.
lore.swsh2-151: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.
lore.swsh2-152: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn't notice the loss.
lore.swsh5-7: The deeper a Cherubi's red, the more nutrients it has stockpiled in its body. And the sweeter and tastier its small ball!
lore.swshp-SWSH088: The faint scent that emanates from its full blossom entices bug Pokémon to it.
lore.swsh5-10: With their large mandibles, these Pokémon can crunch their way through rock. They work together to protect their eggs from Sandaconda.
lore.swsh5-14: It loves the sunshine. When it basks in the sunlight regularly, it grows up with vivid coloration.
lore.swsh5-15: As it slashes into its enemies, it looks like it's dancing. Its elegant appearance has led some to call it the most glamorous Grass Pokémon.
lore.swsh5-16: Although it's called a guardian deity, it's violent enough to crush anyone it sees as an enemy.
lore.swshp-SWSH172: It loves to eat roasted berries, but sometimes it gets too excited and burns them to a crisp.
lore.mcd12-4: When its internal fire flares up, its movements grow sharper and faster. When in trouble, it emits smoke.
lore.swsh5-26: A flame serves as its tongue, melting through the hard shell of Durant so that Heatmor can devour their insides.
lore.swsh5-27: This sneaky Pokémon will slink behind its prey and immobilize it with poisonous gas before the prey even realizes Salandit is there.
lore.swsh5-28: The winner of competitions between Salazzle is decided by which one has the most male Salandit with it.
lore.swsh5-29: It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they're well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.
lore.swsh5-30: While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.
lore.swsh5-34: It can radiate chilliness from the bottoms of its feet. It'll spend the whole day tap-dancing on a frozen floor.
lore.swsh5-35: Its amusing movements make it very popular. It releases its psychic power from the pattern on its belly.
lore.swshp-SWSH089: It traps enemies with its suction-cupped tentacles, then smashes them with its rock-hard head.
lore.swsh5-38: It was originally a Pokémon from afar that escaped to the wild. It can adapt to the dirtiest river.
lore.swsh5-39: A brutish Pokémon that loves to battle. It will crash itself into any foe that approaches its nest.
lore.swsh5-41: Legend has it that the residents of a sunken ancient city changed into these Pokémon.
lore.swsh5-42: Whenever a full moon hangs in the night sky, schools of Jellicent gather near the surface of the sea, waiting for their prey to appear.
lore.swsh5-43: Its skin is thick enough to fend off Mareanie's spikes. With its robust teeth, Bruxish crunches up the spikes and eats them.

lore.swsh2-32: This Pokémon appears just before someone passes away, so it's feared as an emissary of death.

lore.swsh2-46: The vibrating of the bumps all over its body causes earthquake-like tremors. Seismitoad and Croagunk are similar species.
lore.swsh2-57: It stores an overflowing amount of electric energy inside its body. Even a small shock makes it explode.
lore.swsh2-66: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.
lore.swsh2-76: It is extremely good at climbing tree trunks and likes to eat the new sprouts on the trees.

lore.swsh2-82: Once it has whipped up a sandstorm to halt its opponents in their tracks, this terrifying Pokémon snatches away their vitality.

lore.swsh2-99: Its slimy body is hard to grasp. In one region, it is said to have been born from hardened mud.

lore.swsh2-120: Although it's a bit of a ruffian, this Pokémon will take lost Vullaby under its wing and care for them till they're ready to leave the nest.

lore.swsh2-135: In this defensive stance, Aegislash uses its steel body and a force field of spectral power to reduce the damage of any attack.

lore.swsh2-144: It can fly moderately quickly. No matter how far it travels, it can always find its way back to its master and its nest.

lore.swsh2-147: With power equal to an excavator, it can dig through dense bedrock. It's a huge help during tunnel construction.
lore.swsh2-149: Its fluffy fur is a delight to pet, but carelessly reaching out to touch this Pokémon could result in painful retaliation.

lore.swsh3-47: When its anger reaches a breaking point, this Pokémon unleashes a fierce blizzard that freezes every creature around it, be they friend or foe.
lore.swsh3-48: When this Pokémon is in good health, its snot becomes thicker and stickier. It will smear its snot on anyone it doesn't like.
lore.swsh3-49: It swims through frigid seas, searching for prey. From its frozen breath, it forms icy fangs that are harder than steel.
lore.swsh3-50: Individually, they're incredibly weak. It's by gathering up into schools that they're able to confront opponents.
lore.swsh3-55: Rubbing its fleece generates electricity. You'll want to pet it because it's cute, but if you use your bare hand, you'll get a painful shock.
lore.swsh3-57: Its tail shines bright and strong. It has been prized since long ago as a beacon for sailors.
lore.swsh3-59: It stimulates its own muscles with electricity, so it can move quickly. It eases its soreness with electricity, too, so it can recover quickly as well.
lore.swsh3-61: The lightning-wielding guardian deity of Melemele, Tapu Koko is brimming with curiosity and appears before people from time to time.
lore.swsh3-63: Capable of generating 15,000 volts of electricity, this Pokémon looks down on all that would challenge it.
lore.swsh3-67: The songs they sing are totally different depending on the region they live in. Some even sound like they're shouting!
lore.swsh3-68: When it gets angry, it inhales with all its might, and its body gradually inflates. Sometimes they can grow 20 times larger!
lore.swsh3-70: In contrast to its appearance, it's quite timid. When playing with other puppy Pokémon, it sometimes gets bullied.
lore.swsh3-71: Although it's popular with young people, Granbull is timid and sensitive, so it's totally incompetent as a watchdog.
lore.swsh3-73: Though they're still only babies, there's psychic power stored in their ribbonlike feelers, and sometimes they use that power to fight.
lore.swsh3-74: It's said that when stars shine in the night sky, this Pokémon will spirit away sleeping children. Some call it the Witch of Punishment.

lore.swsh3-76: They were sculpted from clay in ancient times. No one knows why, but some of them are driven to continually line up boulders.

lore.swsh3-79: Pokémon living in the forest eat the delicious caps on Morelull's head. The caps regrow overnight.

lore.swsh3-81: It wears a rag fashioned into a Pikachu costume in an effort to look less scary. Unfortunately, the costume only makes it creepier.
lore.swsh3-88: Its body can't be harmed by any sort of attack, so it is very eager to make challenges against enemies.
lore.swsh3-89: Its nest is a sloped, bowl-like pit in the desert. Once something has fallen in, there is no escape.

lore.swsh3-109: While hunting for prey, Zweilous wanders its territory, its two heads often bickering over which way to go.

lore.swsh3-124: They use shells they've stolen from Shelmet to arm and protect themselves. They're very popular Pokémon in the Galar region.
lore.swsh3-129: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.

lore.swsh9-30: If you visit a beach at the end of summer, you'll be able to see groups of Staryu lighting up in a steady rhythm.

lore.swsh4-69: If it finds bad children who won't listen to their parents, it will spirit them away—or so it's said.

lore.swsh9-81: If you see a Sawk training in the mountains in its single-minded pursuit of strength, it's best to quietly pass by.
lore.swsh9-89: Exactly 108 spirits gathered to become this Pokémon. Apparently there are some ill-natured spirits in the mix.

lore.swsh10-60: Tends to prefer people with a chipper disposition to those who are gloomy, but it has shown no discrimination with regard to age or gender. Needs more research.
lore.swsh10-62: True to its honorable-warrior image, it uses the blades on its elbows only in defense of something or someone.
lore.swsh10-63: Said to lure away young children and carry them off to the afterlife. Some whisper that Drifloon are formed of reincarnated human souls, but these rumors are as yet unconfirmed.
lore.swsh10-64: Some say this Pokémon is a collection of souls burdened with regrets, silently drifting through the dusk.
lore.sm6-41: It is said that its emergence gave humans the intelligence to improve their quality of life.
lore.sm6-42: It sleeps at the bottom of a lake. Its spirit is said to leave its body to fly on the lake's surface.
lore.swsh10-67: It is thought that Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf all came from the same egg.
lore.sm6-74: It can instantly create many diamonds by compressing the carbon in the air between its hands.

lore.swsh10-109: Although its fossils can be found in layers of primeval rock, nothing but its face has ever been discovered.

lore.swsh6-116: It was built 20 years ago by scientists who dreamed of exploring space. Their dreams have yet to come true.
lore.swsh6-117: Even though it doesn't die in the vacuum of space, it can't move around very well in zero gravity.
lore.swsh6-118: A faulty update was added to its programming. Its behavior is noticeably strange, so the experiment may have been a failure.
lore.swsh6-122: Its color changes for concealment and also when its mood or health changes. The darker the color, the healthier it is.
lore.swsh6-126: Left alone, its fur will grow longer and longer, but it will only allow someone it trusts to cut it.
lore.swsh6-127: It eats berries nonstop—a habit that has made it more resilient than it looks. It'll show up on farms, searching for yet more berries.
lore.swsh6-128: Common throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon has strong teeth and can chew through the toughest of berry shells.
lore.sv4-1: It secretes a thick, sweet-scented syrup from the tip of its head. It lives on weed-choked ponds.
lore.sv4-2: The antennae have distinctive patterns that look like eyes. When it rains, they grow heavy, making flight impossible.
lore.sv4-8: Its sweat is sweet, like syrup made from boiled- down fruit. Because of this, Bounsweet was highly valued in the past, when sweeteners were scarce.
lore.sv4-18: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.
lore.sv4-19: This Pokémon makes its home near volcanoes. At the end of the day, Magby soaks in magma, resting and recovering from the day's fatigue.
lore.sv4-28: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon's traits match up with an object described in an old book.
lore.sv4-29: It controls flames burning at over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit. It casually swims through the sea of lava it creates by melting rock and sand.
lore.sv4-32: Scales shed by this Pokémon have such a splendorous gleam to them that they've been given to royalty as gifts.
lore.sv4-39: It swims along with a school of Remoraid, and they'll all fight together to repel attackers.
lore.sv4-43: Supposedly, this Pokémon was born from an icicle. It spews out freezing air at −58 degrees Fahrenheit to make itself more comfortable.
lore.sv4-44: It blasts enemies with cold air reaching −148 degrees Fahrenheit, freezing them solid. But it spares their lives afterward—it's a kind Pokémon.
lore.sv4-45: People believe this Pokémon formed when two Vanillish stuck together. Its body temperature is roughly 21 degrees Fahrenheit.
lore.sv4-47: Wimpod gather in swarms, constantly on the lookout for danger. They scatter the moment they detect an enemy's presence.
lore.sv4-49: They live in sunken ships or in holes in the seabed. When Golisopod and Grapploct battle, the loser becomes the winner's meal.
lore.sv4-57: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.
lore.sv4-59: It's not good at storing electricity yet. This Pokémon sneaks into people's homes, looking for electrical outlets to eat electricity from.
lore.sv4-64: Joltik latch on to other Pokémon and suck out static electricity. They're often found sticking to Yamper's hindquarters.
lore.sv4-65: It lays traps of electrified threads near the nests of bird Pokémon, aiming to snare chicks that are not yet good at flying.
lore.sv4-67: The energetic, cheerful dance of these Oricorio is popular with children, but the Oricorio themselves are hard to find in Paldea.
lore.sv4-75: The spirit of a person from a bygone age became this Pokémon. It rambles through ruins, searching for someone who knows its face.
lore.sv4-79: It spends its time running around wastelands. If anyone steals its beloved berries, it will chase them down and exact its revenge.
lore.sv4-81: It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph.
lore.sv4-82: This Pokémon pounds iron scraps together to make a hammer. It will remake the hammer again and again until it's satisfied with the result.
lore.sv4-84: These Pokémon make their homes in piles of scrap metal. They test the strength of each other's hammers by smashing them together.
lore.sv4-85: The hammer tops 220 pounds, yet it gets swung around easily by Tinkaton as it steals whatever it pleases and carries its plunder back home.
lore.sv4-96: Though small, Mienfoo's temperament is fierce. Any creature that approaches Mienfoo carelessly will be greeted with a flurry of graceful attacks.
lore.sv4-97: Delivered at blinding speeds, kicks from this Pokémon can shatter massive boulders into tiny pieces.
lore.sv4-99: This is its form when its shell has fallen off. The color of its core depends on the materials that made up the food it ate.
lore.sv4-107: This mysterious Pokémon has some similarities to a creature that an old book introduced as Slither Wing.
lore.sv4-109: The fear poured into an ancient ritual vessel has clad itself in rocks and dirt to become a Pokémon.
lore.sv4-112: This Pokémon flaps its four wings skillfully. Crobat can fly through cramped caves without needing to slow down.
lore.sv4-114: Opponents that get drawn in by its adorable behavior come away with stinging scratches from its claws and stinging pride from its laughter.
lore.sv4-115: This stealthy Pokémon sneaks up behind prey without making any sound at all. It competes with Thievul for territory.
lore.sv4-117: The toxic liquid it launches from its right arm is so virulent that it can kill a weakened creature instantly.
lore.sv4-127: Mossy caves are their preferred dwellings. Enzymes contained in mosses help Ferroseed's spikes grow big and strong.
lore.sv4-128: Its spikes are harder than steel. This Pokémon crawls across rock walls by stabbing the spikes on its feelers into the stone.
lore.sv4-143: After artificial intelligence was implemented in Porygon2, the Pokémon began using a strange language that only other Porygon2 understand.
lore.sv4-144: Some say an additional program made this Pokémon evolve, but even academics can't agree on whether Porygon-Z is really an evolution.
lore.sv4-147: This Pokémon needs to be milked every day, or else it will fall ill. The flavor of Miltank milk changes with the seasons.
lore.sv4-148: When Whismur cries, the sound of its own voice startles it, making the Pokémon cry even louder. It cries until it's exhausted, then it falls asleep.
lore.sv4-149: The force of this Pokémon's loud voice isn't just the sound—it's also the wave of air pressure that blows opponents away and damages them.
lore.sv4-150: This Pokémon can do more than just shout. To communicate with others of its kind, it'll emit all sorts of sounds from the holes in its body.
lore.sv4-152: It can't relax if it or its surroundings are not clean. It wipes off dirt with its wings.
lore.sm6-1: Six of them together form a full-fledged Pokémon. It's often hunted by Crabrawler, but uses psychokinesis to drive it off.
lore.sm6-17: Using psychic power, it generates a fiery vortex of 5,400 degree Fahrenheit, incinerating foes swept into this whirl of flame.
lore.sm6-27: This calm Pokémon lived in a cold land where there were no violent predators like Tyrantrum.
lore.sm6-28: Using its diamond-shaped crystals, it can instantly create a wall of ice to block an opponent's attack.
lore.sm6-30: The way several Bergmite huddle on its back makes it look like an aircraft carrier made of ice.
lore.sm6-32: When it comes across enemies or potential prey, this Pokémon smashes its water-bubble-covered head into them.
lore.sm6-33: Despite what its appearance suggests, it cares for others. If it finds vulnerable, weak Pokémon, it protectively brings them into its water bubble.
lore.sm6-43: It is thought that Uxie, Mesprit and Azelf all came from the same egg.
lore.sm6-66: They stretch and then contract, yanking their rocks along with them in bold hops. They eat seaweed that washes up on the shoreline.
lore.sm6-67: Barbaracle's legs and hands have minds of their own, and they will move independently. But they usually follow the head's orders.
lore.sm6-68: Its immense jaws have enough destructive force that it can chew up an automobile. It lived 100 million years ago.
lore.sm6-69: Nothing could stop this Pokémon 100 million years ago, so it behaved like a king.
lore.sm6-71: This is Zygarde's form when about 10% of its cells have been gathered. It runs across the land at speeds greater than 60 mph.
lore.sm6-87: When this Pokémon sights its prey, it swirls its ribbonlike feelers as a distraction. A moment later, it pounces.
lore.sm6-89: It inserts its horn into chinks in metal, absorbing metal ions. For some reason, it collects keys.
lore.sm6-91: Its source of protection is its slimy, germ-laden mucous membrane. Anyone who touches it needs some thorough hand-washing.
lore.sm6-93: This Pokémon's mucous can dissolve anything. Toothless, it sprays mucous on its prey. Once they're nicely dissolved, it slurps them up.
lore.sm6-94: It gets picked on because it's meek. But then, whoever teased it gets to feel the full force of its horns and a good swatting from its thick tail.
lore.sm6-96: It is told in mythology that this Pokémon was born before the universe even existed.
lore.sm6-101: The ultrasonic waves it emits from its ears can reduce a large boulder to pebbles. It swoops out of the dark to attack.
lore.swsh4-5: Each of its three heads has its own thoughts. When they want to go in different directions, Exeggutor becomes unable to move.
lore.swsh4-8: It sticks tree bark to itself with its saliva, making itself thicker and larger. Elderly Pineco are ridiculously huge.
lore.swsh4-9: This Pokémon has the ability to move through time. Records describing it as a forest deity can be found from many different eras.
lore.swsh4-13: Because it lived almost entirely underground, it is nearly blind. It uses its antennae instead.
lore.swsh4-14: Its cry leaves a lasting headache if heard for too long. It moves so quickly that it is almost invisible.
lore.swsh4-38: Apparently the itch of its teething impels it to snap its jaws at anything in front of it.
lore.swsh4-39: With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey.
lore.swsh4-40: Cramorant's gluttony led it to try to swallow an Arrokuda whole, which in turn led to Cramorant getting an Arrokuda stuck in its throat.
lore.swsh4-57: One alone can emit only trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.
lore.swsh4-73: While inside a cave, if you look up and see lots of heart-shaped marks lining the walls, it's evidence that Woobat live there.
lore.swsh4-74: Emitting powerful sound waves tires it out. Afterward, it won't be able to fly for a little while.
lore.swsh4-84: It has an easygoing nature. It doesn't care if it bumps its head on boats and boulders while swimming.
lore.swsh4-93: Born when all of Zygarde's cells have been gathered together, it uses force to neutralize those who harm the ecosystem.
lore.swsh4-107: Sandile's still not good at hunting, so it mostly eats things that have collapsed in the desert. It's called "the cleaner of the desert."
lore.swsh4-109: It conceals itself in sandstorms that Flygon whip up and waits patiently for prey to appear.
lore.swsh4-114: In the moment that it gulps down its prey, the inside of its shell is exposed, but to this day, no one has ever seen that sight.
lore.swsh4-116: If you anger it, it will do more than rampage. It will also burst out strong magnetism, causing nearby machines to break.
lore.swsh4-117: It flies at high speeds around the skies. When it finds its prey, Metang takes a firm grip with its sharp claws and never lets go.
lore.swsh4-118: It analyzes its opponents with more accuracy than a supercomputer, which enables it to calmly back them into a corner.
lore.swsh4-119: Once every 1,000 years, the singing of a pure voice will rouse this Pokémon from its near-perpetual slumber. It wakes for only seven days.
lore.swsh4-133: It dislikes cold seasons. They migrate to other lands in search of warmth, flying over 180 miles a day.
lore.swsh4-134: It dives at a steep angle as soon as it spots its prey. It catches its prey with sharp claws.
lore.swsh4-143: It may look spindly, but its neck muscles are heavy-duty. It can peck at a tree 16 times per second!
lore.swsh4-144: From its mouth, it fires the seeds of berries it has eaten. The scattered seeds give rise to new plants.
lore.swsh4-145: Known for forming harmonious couples, this Pokémon is brought to wedding ceremonies as a good luck charm.
